narrative: OMX30 enters Tuesday with constructive overnight tailwinds from US equity strength (NASDAQ +2.26%, S&P +1.49%) and falling rates (US 10Y -70bp to 4.963%), lifting weighted correlation signal to +0.837%. Technicals remain bullish—index sits at 100% of 52W range, +7.6% above 200-MA with MACD above signal and positive momentum (ROC-90 +9.3%)—but Stochastic K=97.8 signals overbought conditions and RSI 63.24 approaches neutral-to-extended territory, raising mean-reversion risk. ADX 18.5 (just above the 18 threshold) provides moderate conviction; watch for consolidation rather than breakout. Copper's +2.32% rally and falling EUR/SEK (-0.40%) benefit exporters, while yield compression pressures real estate and lengthens defensive rotations (Pharma, Essity). Key risk: any reversal in US equity momentum or spike in geopolitical uncertainty (Kremlin forgery scheme narrative) could unwind the risk-on setup quickly.
morningBrief: OMX30 set to open higher on US overnight strength and falling yields, but overbought Stochastic (K=97.8) and extended RSI warrant caution above 3180 (50-MA). Copper's 2.3% jump targets Boliden for cyclical play; watch H&M for EUR/SEK weakness impact (11.24, -40bp). Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) face mixed signals—yield compression offsets NIM support, so size positions cautiously. Industrials (Volvo, Atlas Copco) and Ericsson benefit from weak SEK and NASDAQ sentiment. Real Estate (Balder, Castellum) likely pressured by falling rates. ADX at 18.5 near low threshold; treat moves above 3180 with reduced conviction. US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET is the session's key data point. If risk-off triggers, flight-to-quality favors AstraZeneca and Essity. Range-bound tape likely unless we break 3180 decisively or yields reverse sharply.
